chunks: He said: 'O son of my mother, do not pull me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say that I had created a rift among the Children of Israel and did not pay heed to your command.'

key_terms.ابْنَ أُمَّ: Son of my mother (a term of endearment or respect)

ai.seo_question: What did Aaron say to Moses to explain his actions during the Golden Calf incident?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Aaron (Harun) addresses Moses (Musa) with humility, citing his fear that Moses might accuse him of fracturing the unity of the Children of Israel (*Farraqta bayna Bani Isra'il*) if he were seen as having disobeyed Moses' specific command to maintain peace. Shia scholars, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, interpret this as evidence of Aaron's *Ijtihad* and strategic patience (*Sabr*), noting that he was not sinning but rather managing the idolatrous crowd until Moses' return, thus preserving the community's cohesion.
